failures.criterion: The architect's line 2: no line of docs/ says a launch replaces a drifted issue pod. Three of the facets this change moved out of a launch's reach are still documented as a launch's.
failures.evidence:
`docs/kubernetes.md`, section 'A pod whose address moved' (line 2924), lines 2966 to 2967:

  'A pod whose launcher dials a stale stream, **which lacks the broker enrollment its roles are started against now, or which lacks the operator mount holding a file `role_config_files` names for any of its roles**, cannot run them as a pod created now would, and every role of it is reported at once, from the boot that re-adopts them: the first of them relaunched replaces the pod…'

The broker enrollment and the role overlays are two of the three facets this change moved from `movedInPod` into `driftedInPod` (`addresses.go`), so for an issue pod a launch no longer replaces for either: it keeps the pod and the round replaces it. My own round-1 and round-2 red tests hold exactly that and both pass at this head (TestARoleStartedInAKeptDriftedPodIsStartedAsItsPodWasBuilt, whose two rows are the enrollment and a named role's overlay). The sentence that follows is right and shows the distinction the paragraph misses: 'The controller's pod, whose one launcher dials a stale stream, or which lacks the broker enrollment…, is replaced the same way at its relaunch' — true, because no round covers the controller's pod (`roundCovers`). The issue-pod sentence before it is the false one. The branch's own diff of docs/kubernetes.md (129 changed lines) does not touch this paragraph.

A second line of the same kind, line 1968: 'every pod created after that apply gets 50 GiB and **a pod already running keeps the size it started with until a launch replaces it**'. The disk size is one of the five keys of the `legion.dev/pod-shape` record this change added, so an issue pod whose `issue_volume` moved is replaced by its round, not by a launch. This one is weaker — before this change nothing read the disk size at all, so the sentence was loose rather than false — but it names the wrong mechanism for a key this change created, in a file the change now edits.

The rest of the sweep is clean, and I read every candidate rather than grepping alone. The section the last round fixed is right throughout: 'no launch replaces a live pod for an image change alone', `warnImageDrift`'s line now ends 'until its update round replaces the pod', the round's own paragraph is accurate, the controller's pod is given to its launch with `roundCovers` and `shapeDrift` named, and the `movedInPod` list of what a launch does replace matches the code. The other `launch replaces` hits are each another subject and each true: the layout before one container (1667), a failed init container (3025), the disk shape before the pod-owned disk (1256, 1532), and the three-way list at 3797, which gives drift to the round in as many words.
